# Domain-Join → OrgPath-Join Crosswalk {.unnumbered}

When a PC or server runs `Add-Computer -DomainName contoso.com` (or the GUI
equivalent), a single action silently establishes **a dozen-plus governance
facts** about that machine: an identity, a trust relationship, a place in the
org tree, a policy inheritance path, a name in DNS, a machine certificate, and
more. Operators rarely enumerate them because domain-join bundles them into one
opaque transaction.

Modernizing to the cloud does **not** remove the need for those governance
facts — it removes the single bundling mechanism. The **OrgPath join** is the
deliberate, governed process that reproduces each *intent* with a cloud-native
carrier. This document does two things:

1. **Part A** enumerates everything an AD domain-join creates or establishes.
2. **Part B** gives the corresponding OrgPath-join process — phase by phase,
   per device class (client vs server) — including DNS and certificates.

The spine of the mapping is the canonical
[`computer-object-crosswalk.yaml`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/computer-object-crosswalk.yaml)
(`UIAO_GAE_CROSSWALK`, ADR-031); this guide makes it operator-readable and adds
the DNS and PKI surfaces.

::: {.callout-important}
## The governing principle: reproduce intent, not mechanism

Do not try to recreate domain-join in the cloud. **Regenerate from the
governance intent** (the same doctrine the GPO Sunset Program uses for policy).
A computer object's *intent* is "this machine has an identity, a place, a
policy set, a name, and a trust boundary" — each of those gets a distinct,
purpose-built cloud carrier, and several deliberately become **non-machine**
constructs (a workload identity is an app, not a computer account).
:::

## Part A — What an AD domain-join establishes

A domain-join is not one fact; it is this set, created at join time or shortly
after (via the first GPO/autoenrollment cycle):

### A.1 Identity & trust

| # | Established at join | What it really is |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Computer account object** | A SID-backed **security principal** in `CN=Computers` (or the redirected OU) — the machine can authenticate as itself |
| 2 | **Machine password + secure channel** | A rotating shared secret establishing the `Netlogon` secure channel to a DC; the basis of all machine auth |
| 3 | **Kerberos machine identity** | The computer account's keys; the machine gets a TGT and can request service tickets |
| 4 | **Service Principal Names (SPNs)** | `HOST/<name>`, `HOST/<fqdn>`, and any service SPNs — how Kerberos clients locate services on the box |
| 5 | **Trust boundary / domain membership** | The machine is "inside" — it trusts domain DCs, honors domain policy, and is trusted by domain resources |

### A.2 Organizational placement & policy

| # | Established at join | What it really is |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | **OU placement (Distinguished Name)** | The computer object lands in an OU — its position in the x.500 tree, which *is* its organizational identity |
| 7 | **GPO inheritance** | Every GPO linked to that OU (and parents) applies — Computer Configuration, security baselines, drive/printer maps, scripts |
| 8 | **Group memberships** | `Domain Computers` at minimum; often security groups used for GPO filtering or resource access |
| 9 | **Delegation / ACLs** | The object inherits OU ACLs; specific admins may be delegated rights over it (reset, manage) |
| 10 | **Local-admin policy (LAPS)** | A GPO-delivered LAPS policy randomizes and escrows the local admin password |

### A.3 Name resolution, certificates, time

| # | Established at join | What it really is |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | **Dynamic DNS registration** | The host registers its **A** (and the DHCP/host registers **PTR**) record in AD-integrated DNS via secure dynamic update; it gets the primary **DNS suffix** of the domain |
| 12 | **DC/service location** | The machine resolves `_ldap._tcp`, `_kerberos._tcp` **SRV** records to find DCs — name resolution *is* the control-plane locator |
| 13 | **Machine certificate (autoenrollment)** | The autoenrollment GPO + an ADCS **certificate template** issue a machine/computer certificate (used for 802.1X, IPsec, RDP, etc.) with no user action |
| 14 | **Time hierarchy** | `W32Time` syncs up the domain hierarchy (PDC emulator at the root) — Kerberos depends on it |

### A.4 Lifecycle & inventory

| # | Established at join | What it really is |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | **Inventory / discovery anchor** | The computer object is the authoritative directory record SCCM, monitoring, and audits key off |
| 16 | **Workload-identity host** | The box can host **GMSAs**, **Kerberos constrained delegation**, and machine-context service auth |

**The point:** join created identity (1–5), placement & policy (6–10), name +
cert + time (11–14), and lifecycle/inventory/workload anchors (15–16) — in one
step. OrgPath-join reproduces each, intentionally, with the right carrier.

## The master crosswalk

Every AD construct maps to a cloud-native carrier on one of four **planes**
(identity, management, governance, workload). This table is the operator view
of `computer-object-crosswalk.yaml`; the **Track** column is the migration
track and `(blocker)` marks a construct whose migration must complete before AD
can be retired.

| AD construct | Cloud-native carrier | Plane | XW / Track |
|---|---|---|---|
| Computer account as **security principal** | Service Principal / Managed Identity / Workload Identity — the machine stops being a security principal | workload | XW-001 · T3 *(blocker)* |
| Computer object as **device identity** | **Entra Device** (Joined/Registered) — a token anchor for PRT + Conditional Access, **not** a security principal | identity | XW-002 · T1 |
| **OU placement** (Distinguished Name) | **OrgPath** (`extensionAttribute1..10` for Entra, ARM tags for Arc) + dynamic groups + Intune scope tags | governance | XW-003 · T1 |
| **GPO** via OU hierarchy | Intune config profiles / Settings Catalog / security baselines (clients); Azure Policy (Arc servers) — scoped by OrgPath, not OUs | management | XW-004 · T1 |
| **Delegation / OU ACLs** | Entra RBAC + PIM + **Administrative Units** with OrgPath-driven membership | governance | XW-005 · T1 |
| **SPNs** | App Registration + Service Principal + OAuth2/OIDC endpoints (each SPN catalogued + rebuilt) | workload | XW-006 · T3 *(blocker)* |
| **Kerberos constrained delegation** | App-to-app OAuth2 / API permissions / managed identities (rebuilt per service) | workload | XW-007 · T3 *(blocker)* |
| **Machine Kerberos auth to resources** | Device-based Conditional Access + app tokens + managed identities | identity | XW-008 · T3 |
| **Computer object as inventory anchor** | Intune device record (clients) / **Azure Arc machine** (servers) — split inventory, reconciled by the survey adapter | management | XW-009 · T2 |
| **Config management** (GPO + SCCM) | Intune (clients) / Arc extensions + Azure Policy (servers) | management | XW-010 · T1/T2 |
| **Local-admin / LAPS** | Intune Local Admin policies + **Entra LAPS** | management | XW-011 · T1 |
| **Domain membership / trust boundary** | Entra Join (clients) / Arc + Entra-join, **non-domain-joined** (servers, ADR-002); AD-join is the *last* thing removed | identity | XW-012 · T1/T3 *(blocker)* |
| **GMSAs** | Managed Identity (system- or user-assigned); on-prem GMSA users are per-workload tasks | workload | XW-013 · T3 *(blocker)* |

**Two structural truths fall out of this table:**

1. **The machine stops being a security principal.** The single biggest
   conceptual shift: a domain computer authenticates *as itself* (XW-001).
   In the cloud the Entra device object is **only** a token anchor for
   Conditional Access (XW-002) — workloads authenticate as **apps / managed
   identities**, not as the box. This is why SPNs, KCD, and GMSAs (XW-006/007/013)
   are *retirement blockers*: each is real work, not a flag flip.
2. **Servers and clients diverge.** Clients Entra-join immediately (Track 1).
   Servers **stay AD-joined** until their workload identities migrate
   (XW-012, Track 3), then cut over to **Arc + Entra-join, non-domain-joined**
   (ADR-002). OrgPath rides both: `extensionAttribute1..10` on the Entra device
   for clients, ARM **tags** on the Arc machine for servers.

# Part B — The OrgPath-join process

Domain-join was one transaction; OrgPath-join is a **governed sequence**. Like
the Intune + Azure Arc deployment, it drives every device to the **same
destination — a stamped, governed OrgPath — regardless of where it starts.**
Three entry states feed one end-state:

| Entry state | Path | How OrgPath is established | Primary tooling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brand-new device | **New Join → Entra OrgPath** (B.1) | Assigned at procurement, stamped at enrollment (Intune-First 5-phase) | Autopilot / ABM / Zero-Touch / Arc onboarding |
| Existing **AD domain-joined** | **AD → Entra OrgPath** (B.2) | **Derived from AD** (OU + attributes), then the box sheds domain-join | `uiao orgtree assess`, GPO Sunset (ADR-080) |
| Already **Entra/Arc, no OrgPath** | **Already-Entra → Entra OrgPath** (B.3) | **Captured + backfilled** (brownfield) | `uiao orgtree inventory` |

All three converge on the identical **common end-state (B.4–B.9)**: OrgPath
stamped on the device object/resource, dynamic-group membership, policy,
certificates, DNS, and modern authentication. And **within every path the
client-vs-server plane divergence holds** — Entra device object + Graph
`extensionAttributes` for clients, Arc machine + ARM `tags` for servers —
exactly the two writeback planes from the Intune (Graph) and Arc (ARM) deployment
guides.

```
   New device ─────┐
   (procure)       │
                   ▼
   AD-joined ──► [ OrgPath join ] ──► stamp ─► groups ─► policy ─► certs ─► DNS ─► auth ─► validate
   (assess)        ▲                  (B.4)    (B.5)     (B.5)     (B.6)    (B.7)   (B.8)    (B.9)
                   │
   Entra, no ──────┘
   OrgPath
   (inventory)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## The OrgPath source-precedence chain (IFO_001 §5)

Every later step depends on the device carrying a valid OrgPath. The value is
resolved by a strict precedence chain, and a source counts only if it is
non-empty **and** resolves to a `Status: Active` node in the OrgTree registry:

1. **Procurement record** (authoritative) — set on the PO.
2. **Hardware-hash mapping CSV** (e.g. `governance/autopilot/orgpath-mapping.csv`).
3. **Primary-user derivation** — the provisioning user's OrgPath (BYOD / pre-doctrine).
4. **`/UNPOSITIONED`** — terminal quarantine; the device is governed but blocked
   from resources until positioned.

This guarantees *every* enrolled device has a non-empty OrgPath at the moment
compliance and network-admission evaluation begins.
:::

## B.1 Path A — New Join → Entra OrgPath (net-new devices)

The canonical **Intune-First five-phase** onboarding (`IFO_002`, ADR-071):
Procure → Pre-stage → Position → Provision → Validate. It binds organizational
position *before the device exists* — the cure for AD's drift-prone,
after-the-fact OU placement. Phases 1–3 are below; **Position, Provision, and
Validate are the common end-state** (B.4–B.9), shared with the other two paths.

### Phase 1 — Procure (replaces: ad-hoc OU placement)

Before hardware is ordered, the purchase request carries the **OrgPath** and the
resolved `OrgNodeId`, validated against the OrgTree registry. The procurement
record is committed to the governance repo. *This is the cloud replacement for
"an admin drops the new computer object into an OU"* — except it is decided by
policy, reviewed, and recorded, not improvised after the box powers on.

- **Gate:** OrgPath valid on the PO and resolves to an Active node.
- **Carrier:** the procurement record (`governance/procurement/orders/{PO}.json`).

### Phase 2 — Pre-stage (replaces: pre-staged computer object / `djoin`)

The vendor-program record is stamped with the OrgPath so the device is governed
*before first boot*:

| Device class | Pre-stage carrier |
|---|---|
| Windows client | **Windows Autopilot** group tag |
| macOS / iOS | **Apple Business Manager** device note / ADE profile |
| Android | **Zero-Touch** / KME config JSON |
| Server (Arc) | **Arc resource tag** on the pre-created resource / onboarding script |

The hardware hash (or serial) → OrgPath mapping is pre-staged so Phase 4 can
stamp deterministically. This is the cloud analogue of offline-domain-join
(`djoin /provision`) — the identity intent exists before the OS does.

### Phase 3 — Join / Enroll (replaces: `Add-Computer -DomainName`)

This is the actual "join," and it is **where clients and servers diverge**. The
two sub-flows below are referenced by Path B as well (an AD-joined device that
migrates runs the same join mechanics).

#### Client — Entra Join (ADR-001)

The client **Entra-joins** (cloud-only; **no Hybrid Azure AD Join** — HAADJ is
deprecated per ADR-001) and auto-enrolls in Intune via Autopilot. The Entra
**device object** is created — a token anchor for Primary Refresh Token +
Conditional Access, **not** a security principal (XW-002). No domain membership,
no DC line-of-sight, no GPO.

> HAADJ is a dead-end, not an interim state. Existing HAADJ devices are
> **wiped & re-provisioned** to reach Entra-joined (ADR-001).

#### Server — hard cutover to Arc (ADR-002)

Servers do **not** Entra-join like clients. Per ADR-002 this is a **hard
cutover, not a gradual hybrid**:

1. Inventory every Kerberos-dependent service and SPN/KCD/GMSA on the box first
   (these are retirement blockers — B.10).
2. Migrate those services to modern auth / managed identities.
3. Replicate the box's GPO settings to Azure Policy / Arc configuration.
4. Upgrade to **Windows Server 2025+** (required for `AADLoginForWindows`).
5. **Unjoin from AD → install the Arc agent → deploy `AADLoginForWindows`.** The
   machine becomes Microsoft Entra **joined via Arc** and can no longer join any
   domain.
6. Assign **Azure RBAC** roles (`Virtual Machine Administrator Login` /
   `Virtual Machine User Login`) — these replace domain/local group membership
   for RDP access.
7. Validate access, then disable the AD computer object.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Server-class caveats (as of June 2026, ADR-002)

- **Windows Server 2019/2022** can be **Arc-managed** but **cannot** use
  `AADLoginForWindows` — they stay AD-joined temporarily (Exception Path C).
- **Conditional Access cannot yet target Arc-enrolled server logins**, and
  **Entra LAPS is unavailable** for Arc servers. Plan compensating controls.
:::

## B.2 Path B — AD → Entra OrgPath (existing domain-joined fleet)

These devices already carry the **entire Part A footprint** — a computer object,
an OU placement, GPOs, a machine cert, DNS records. The OrgPath-join doesn't
invent their position; it **derives it from what AD already knows**, then sheds
the domain-join machinery.

1. **Derive OrgPath from AD.** `uiao orgtree assess` reads the AD computer (and
   user) objects — OU, `department`, `physicalDeliveryOfficeName`, etc. — and
   maps them onto OrgPath facets (the AD→facet mapping). This is the existing-
   fleet counterpart to procurement: the OU tree *becomes* the OrgPath
   (`UIAO_156` OU→Entra Migration Runbook). No procurement record is needed.
2. **Migrate the join.** Run the Phase 3 join mechanics (B.1 §Phase 3): clients
   **Entra-join** (wipe & re-provision any HAADJ, ADR-001); servers **hard-cut
   over to Arc** (ADR-002). The domain-join footprint (Part A #1–16) is shed as
   the box leaves the domain.
3. **Retire GPO.** The **GPO Sunset Program** (ADR-080) replaces OU-linked GPOs
   with OrgPath dynamic-group-targeted Intune profiles (clients) / Azure Policy
   on Arc tags (servers). *Regenerate from policy intent — do not copy GPOs 1:1.*

Then the device enters the **common end-state** (B.4): its derived OrgPath is
written to the new Entra device object / Arc machine, and every governance intent
from Part A is re-established on a cloud carrier.

::: {.callout-note}
The two clocks can run independently: derive + stamp OrgPath (steps 1 → B.4)
**before** you finish retiring GPOs (step 3) — in fact you must, because the GPO
Sunset's dynamic-group targeting depends on the OrgPath attributes existing
first.
:::

## B.3 Path C — Already-Entra-only → Entra OrgPath (brownfield backfill)

Devices that are **already Entra-joined or Arc-enrolled but were never stamped**
with OrgPath — the gap our deployment guides' brownfield case covers. There is
no re-join and no migration; there is only **capture and backfill**:

1. **Capture.** `uiao orgtree inventory --from-graph --from-arm` scans both
   planes (Entra device `extensionAttributes` + Arc machine `tags`). A device
   missing OrgPath surfaces as a **`DRIFT-IDENTITY`** finding — that finding list
   *is* the worklist.
2. **Propose.** The collector proposes a backfill for the missing facets via the
   source chain (`--asset-map` → `--owner-map`, i.e. CMDB/procurement then
   primary-user derivation), validated against the Codebook; anything it can't
   resolve is bucketed for manual review — never auto-guessed.
3. **Backfill.** Resolved devices flow into the **common end-state** (B.4) via
   `assess --write`; the same idempotent reconcile loop holds them stamped.

```bash
uiao orgtree inventory --from-graph --from-arm --subscription <sub> \
  --owner-map owners.json --snapshot-out snap.json --worklist-out worklist.json
```

# Part B (cont.) — The common end-state

Everything below is **identical for all three paths** and for both device
classes (only the carrier differs: Graph `extensionAttributes` vs ARM `tags`).
This is the cloud reconstruction of the Part A footprint.

## B.4 Stamp OrgPath (replaces #6 OU placement) — ADR-038

Write the resolved OrgPath onto the device's cloud object — the device-plane
writeback from the Intune/Arc deployment guides:

| Device class | Carrier | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Entra client | `onPremisesExtensionAttributes.extensionAttribute1..10` | Graph `PATCH /devices/{id}` (`ArmTransport`'s Graph sibling) |
| Arc server | `tags.Region`, `tags.Department`, … | ARM `PATCH {resourceId}?api-version=…` |

A device whose OrgPath cannot be resolved lands on **`/UNPOSITIONED`** —
governed but quarantined (B.8) until positioned. This *is* "Phase 4 — Provision /
Position" of the Intune-First flow.

## B.5 Policy & delegation (replaces #7 GPO, #9 OU ACLs, #11 LAPS)

- **Policy:** OrgPath-driven **dynamic groups** (`UIAO_152`) materialize every
  subtree; **Intune** configuration/compliance profiles (clients) and **Azure
  Policy** (Arc servers) are assigned to those groups via `policy-targets.yaml`
  (ADR-039). This replaces GPO-by-OU with attribute-driven, PR-reviewed targeting
  (XW-004/XW-010).
- **Delegation:** **Administrative Units** (`UIAO_154`) — configured as
  **Restricted Management** AUs — with OrgPath-driven membership replace
  OU-scoped delegation; admins get Entra roles scoped to the AU, not the OU
  (XW-005).
- **Local admin:** **Entra LAPS** + Intune endpoint-security policy replace
  GPO-LAPS (XW-011) — *clients only* (unavailable for Arc servers, B.3).

## B.6 Certificates (replaces #13 ADCS autoenrollment) — UIAO-PKI-MOD-001

GPO-driven ADCS autoenrollment of a machine cert becomes **Intune certificate
profiles** targeted by OrgPath dynamic group:

- **Trust:** an Intune **Trusted Root** profile distributes the issuing CA chain.
- **Issuance:** an Intune **SCEP** (or **PKCS**) profile issues a per-device cert
  from **Microsoft Cloud PKI** (full-cloud or **BYOCA** under your existing root),
  or from on-prem **ADCS via the Certificate Connector / NDES** during transition.
- **Strong mapping (KB5014754):** SCEP from Cloud PKI auto-includes the SID URI
  SAN (`tag:microsoft.com,2022-09-14:sid:<SID>`); PKCS needs Connector
  v6.2406+. Hybrid devices need `onPremisesSecurityIdentifier` synced.
- **OrgPath-in-cert:** for NAC, the device's OrgPath is written into the cert
  **SAN OtherName** (ADR-073) so an 802.1X RADIUS server can read it directly.
- **User auth:** **Entra CBA** (PIV/CAC against the Federal Common Policy CA
  chain) + **Windows Hello for Business** replace smart-card-on-domain.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Domain Controller certificates stay on ADCS (BRIDGE).** Cloud PKI cannot issue
the KDC Authentication EKU, so DC certs are enrolled by domain-joined DCs via
ADCS autoenrollment until AD is decommissioned. The **PKI/CA observation
adapter** (`pki-ca`) that would inventory CA health is a **reserved** slot, not
yet implemented.
:::

## B.7 DNS (replaces #11 dynamic DNS, #12 DC-locator SRV) — UIAO-DNS-MOD-001

A domain-joined host self-registers an **A** record (DHCP registers **PTR**) via
secure dynamic update, and finds DCs via `_ldap/_kerberos` **SRV** records. In
the cloud target:

- **Name registration:** Azure VMs register via **Azure DNS Private Zone
  auto-registration**; physical/on-prem devices keep using **on-prem DHCP/DNS**.
  Hybrid resolution flows through the **Azure DNS Private Resolver** (inbound/
  outbound endpoints + **forwarding rulesets**); **split-brain** zones serve
  internal vs external answers.
- **IPAM governance:** **Infoblox** (Federal-Preferred) or **BlueCat** adapters
  give API-driven DNS/DHCP record management across both estates.
- **DC-locator SRV records remain on AD-integrated DNS** for the whole migration
  (they locate the DCs that still exist); they are decommissioned only after a
  30-day validation gate when AD itself retires.

## B.8 Authentication & network trust (replaces #2/#3 secure channel & Kerberos) — ADR-068

The Netlogon secure channel and machine Kerberos give way to cloud auth:

- **Cloud Kerberos Trust** issues Entra-backed Kerberos TGTs so Entra-joined /
  Arc devices reach **legacy** file-share / print / SQL resources **without** an
  on-prem domain join.
- **Entra CBA + passwordless** (FIDO2 / WHfB) are the modern path; **NTLM
  elimination is mandatory by 2027-04-01** (Notice 0009); rollout is privileged
  accounts → service accounts (workload-identity-federation, ADR-004) →
  non-privileged users **by OrgPath segment**.
- **Device-based Conditional Access** (the Entra device object as token anchor,
  XW-002/XW-008) replaces "computer Kerberos ticket = trusted."
- **Network admission:** at 802.1X the RADIUS server reads the device's OrgPath
  (from the cert SAN, B.6) and returns the VLAN / dACL / posture per
  `UIAO_012`. A **`/UNPOSITIONED`** device lands on the **quarantine VLAN** at the
  port — *before* compliance evaluation.

## B.9 Validate (the gate AD never had) — IFO_002 Phase 5

Domain-join had no success gate; OrgPath-join does. Confirm: the **stamped
OrgPath equals the intended OrgPath**, the device is in the **expected dynamic
groups**, compliance is green, certs issued, and DNS resolves. Persist the
`GovernanceReport` as evidence (`uiao orgtree govern --out`). Drift after this
point re-trips `DRIFT-IDENTITY` and the reconcile loop converges it.

## B.10 Workload identities — the retirement blockers

The machine **stops being a security principal**. Everything it did *as itself*
moves to non-machine constructs, and until each is migrated **AD cannot be
retired** (Track 3, `retirement_blocker: true`):

| AD construct | Becomes | XW |
|---|---|---|
| SPNs | App Registration + Service Principal (OAuth2/OIDC) | XW-006 |
| Kerberos constrained delegation | App-to-app OAuth2 / managed identities | XW-007 |
| GMSAs | Managed Identity (system/user-assigned) | XW-013 |
| Machine security principal | Workload identity / WIF (ADR-004) | XW-001 |

These are catalogued per box during Path B step 2 (the server cutover inventory)
and rebuilt per service — there is no flag-flip.

# Part C — Quick-reference

## C.1 DNS / Certificate / Auth crosswalk (the surfaces beyond the YAML)

The master table covered the computer-object functions; these are the DNS, PKI,
and auth surfaces a domain-join also establishes.

| Domain-join establishes | Cloud-native carrier | Canon |
|---|---|---|
| Dynamic **A/PTR** registration (secure dynamic update) | Azure DNS Private Zone auto-registration (Azure VMs) / on-prem DHCP retained; DNS Private Resolver for hybrid | UIAO-DNS-MOD-001 |
| **DC-locator SRV** records | Remain on AD DNS through migration; resolver forwarding rulesets; retired post-AD | UIAO-DNS-MOD-001 |
| **Conditional forwarders** / split-horizon | DNS forwarding rulesets + Private/Public zones (split-brain); Infoblox / BlueCat IPAM | UIAO-DNS-MOD-001 |
| **Machine certificate** via ADCS autoenrollment GPO | Intune Trusted Root + SCEP/PKCS profile from Cloud PKI (or ADCS via Certificate Connector), OrgPath-targeted | UIAO-PKI-MOD-001 |
| **DC / KDC certificates** | Stay on ADCS (BRIDGE) — Cloud PKI can't issue KDC EKU | UIAO-PKI-MOD-001 §8.1 |
| **Smart-card / user cert auth** | Entra CBA (FPKI chain) + Windows Hello for Business | ADR-068, UIAO-PKI-MOD-001 §7 |
| **Secure channel + machine Kerberos** | Cloud Kerberos Trust (legacy) + device-based Conditional Access | ADR-068, XW-008 |
| **NTLM** | Eliminated by 2027-04-01 (Notice 0009) | ADR-068 |
| **W32Time** domain hierarchy | Cloud/host time (no domain time hierarchy) | — |
| **802.1X via machine cert/NTLM** | OrgPath read from cert SAN → RADIUS VLAN/dACL; `/UNPOSITIONED` → quarantine | UIAO_012, ADR-073 |

## C.2 Client join checklist (Entra)

1. OrgPath on PO (new) / derived from AD (migrate) / inventory finding (brownfield).
2. Autopilot group-tag pre-stage (new) or wipe-&-reprovision from HAADJ (migrate).
3. **Entra Join** + Intune auto-enroll (no HAADJ).
4. Stamp OrgPath → `extensionAttribute1..10` (Graph).
5. Dynamic-group membership → Intune profiles + compliance; Entra LAPS.
6. Trusted Root + SCEP cert (Cloud PKI), OrgPath in SAN.
7. Cloud Kerberos Trust / CBA; device-based Conditional Access.
8. Validate stamped == intended; evidence committed.

## C.3 Server join checklist (Arc)

1. Inventory SPNs / KCD / GMSA / Kerberos services (B.10 blockers) — migrate them.
2. Replicate GPO → Azure Policy; upgrade to **Server 2025+**.
3. **Unjoin AD → Arc agent → `AADLoginForWindows`** (hard cutover).
4. Azure RBAC `Virtual Machine Administrator/User Login` (replaces RDP-by-Kerberos).
5. Stamp OrgPath → ARM `tags` (ARM resource ID required).
6. Azure Policy assigned by OrgPath tags; SCEP cert if needed.
7. Validate; disable AD computer object.
8. *(Caveats: 2019/2022 = Arc-managed only; no CA on Arc logins; no Entra LAPS.)*

## C.4 Status — implemented vs doctrine vs reserved

| Surface | Status |
|---|---|
| OrgPath device-plane writeback (Graph + ARM, incl. brownfield `inventory`) | **Implemented** |
| `uiao orgtree assess` (AD → facets) / `govern` (drift) | **Implemented** |
| Dynamic groups (UIAO_152), Administrative Units (UIAO_154) | **Implemented (canon)** |
| Intune policy targeting (UIAO_011) | **Implemented** |
| DNS modernization (UIAO-DNS-MOD-001), PKI modernization (UIAO-PKI-MOD-001) | **Adopted (Tier 1 doctrine)** |
| Entra-join-only (ADR-001), Arc hard-cutover (ADR-002), auth modernization (ADR-068) | **Accepted doctrine** |
| Azure Policy-for-Arc authoring, Intune profile authoring, PKI/CA observation (`pki-ca`) | **Reserved** (per-adapter ADR pending) |
| AD Computer Object Conversion Guide (ADR-042) | **Draft** |

::: {.callout-important}
## Known gaps (June 2026)

- **Conditional Access cannot target Arc-enrolled server logins**, and **Entra
  LAPS is unavailable** for Arc servers (ADR-002).
- **DC/KDC certs and DC-locator SRV records remain on AD** until full
  decommission — they are BRIDGE, not migrable.
- **Policy/profile authoring and Azure-Policy-for-Arc are reserved adapters** —
  OrgPath writes the attributes/tags; you author the policies in Intune/Azure
  directly until those activate.
- OrgPath itself has **no production adopters** yet (Tier-3+ doctrine): pilot,
  dry-run, and smoke-test single devices first.
:::
